Wenyu Chiou

Behavioral simulation, AI evaluation, and the systems that make agents trustworthy

Research engineer for LLM evaluation, agent systems, and computational social science.

I design evaluation systems for large language model applications and agent-based simulations. My work connects human decision data, computational social science, and fail-closed engineering — from a 937-household survey to 52,141 simulated households and open-source AI tooling.

Open to Summer 2027 internships in AI research, LLM evaluation, agent development, and computational social science.

01

Selected engineering

research-hub

Maintained open-source tool

Literature workflows are repetitive and easy to get subtly wrong across tools. research-hub turns Zotero, Obsidian, and NotebookLM into one AI-operable workspace — searching, ingesting, and syncing papers through a single CLI, MCP server, and REST API.

Case study →

codex-delegate

Maintained open-source tool

Delegating code work to a second AI agent is only economical if the delegate cannot fabricate success. codex-delegate verifies the delegate’s completion from git state rather than from its own report.

Case study →

awesome-agentic-ai-zh

Maintained open-source tool

Chinese-speaking learners lacked a staged path into agentic AI, and hand-mirrored translations drift. This trilingual curriculum keeps its locales verifiably in sync with CI.

5K+ GitHub stars, 700+ forks (August 2026)

02

Selected research

LLM evaluation study

In preparation

Plausible LLM responses are not evidence that an agent reproduces human decisions. This two-arm study compares human survey pathways with responses generated from label-blind socioeconomic personas across social groups.

Case study →

FLOODABM

Research prototype

Flood-adaptation models usually assert household behavior instead of measuring it. FLOODABM grounds 52,141 simulated households in a 937-household survey and validates losses against observed insurance claims.

Case study →

Cat_framework

Research prototype

A loss number without an inspectable validation chain cannot be trusted. This Hazus-based seismic bridge-loss pipeline reports where the recipe fails, not only where it works.

Case study →

The full research program →

Current focus: evaluation and governance methods for LLM agents — testing whether they reproduce real human decision pathways (grounded in a 937-household survey I designed and fielded) and constraining agent-driven simulations so they stay trustworthy. Research software in preparation for release.
